headline: Macro favors Capital (Labor Share 93.7, Profits/Wages +7.5%); Equities show 3M pullback in AI hardware (-17.91%) vs. IT/Staffing bounce (+2.77%)

bullets.title: Labor Share Compression
bullets.text: BLS Nonfarm Labor Share stands at 93.73 (-0.67% QoQ, -1.60% YoY), remaining structurally below the 2017=100 baseline.
bullets.reason: Real output growth is accruing to capital owners faster than compensation: nonfarm payrolls sit at 159.3M with average weekly hours capped at 34.4h and hourly earnings at $38.00/hr.

bullets.title: Profits Outpacing Wages
bullets.text: Corporate Profits-to-Wage-Bill ratio hit 0.404 (+7.50% QoQ, +22.00% YoY).
bullets.reason: BEA Corporate Profits expanded to $4,279.9B SAAR (+8.40% QoQ, +26.61% YoY) while the annualized private wage bill grew only +0.47% MoM (+4.30% YoY) to $10,827.8B.

bullets.title: Watchlist Spread Drivers
bullets.text: 3M Watchlist Spread is -20.68pp (Capital Enablers -17.91% vs. Labor-Heavy +2.77%).
bullets.reason: Short-term multiple compression hit AI hardware/power names (VRT (-32.6%), SMCI (-26.1%), NVDA (-24.5%)), while oversold IT outsourcers & staffing rebounded (EPAM (+63.7%), CTSH (+12.3%), RHI (+4.9%)). Over 1Y, hardware/grid winners (GEV (+37.8%), TSM (+35.7%), ANET (+34.8%)) still anchor the capex cycle.

bullets.title: AI & Power Capex Catalyst
bullets.text: "10-year data center moratorium approved in Ottawa, Kansas" (Data Center Dynamics).
bullets.reason: Compute & silicon capex expansion shifting income toward capital owners. Also tracked: "Quantinuum upgrades quantum computer at Riken, partners with SoftBank for AI data center deployments" (Data Center Dynamics).

bullets.title: Workforce & Macro Signal
bullets.text: "US labor market remains resilient, though AI-driven layoffs continue" (Anadolu Ajansı) — with U.S. unemployment at 4.1% (2026-10-01).
bullets.reason: Direct headcount reduction / AI substitution compressing labor share.
